01 The fire

One trough. Oak only. No gas, ever.

Tomas Reyes lights the trough at 11:00 and again at 17:00 with oak lump charcoal from one yard upriver. Nothing touches a flame: everything cooks over coals gone white, two hands above the bars, turned by hand.

5 mof trough, open to the counter
400°at the bars, white coals
90 kgof oak charcoal a night

The counter opens at 12:00 and the garden at 18:00, Tuesday to Sunday.

Closed Mondays · the pit is cleaned

The board. Priced by the portion.

Every portion is weighed raw. Cuts come with grilled lemon and flaky salt; skewers on flatbread with sumac onions. Tap + and it goes on your table below.

Lamb chops

Salted an hour before. Four minutes a side on white coals, rested six. Pink at the bone.

04 The whole lamb

A whole lamb for a table of twelve.

One lamb from the downs, 16 to 18 kilos, rubbed the night before and hung over the coals for six hours on the day. It rests forty minutes, comes to the garden on a platter of saffron rice with almonds and raisins, and is carved at your table. Salads, flatbread and the ember vegetables come with it.

For a table at 20:00, the lamb goes on the coals at 13:20.

05 The garden

At night, the garden.

Six long tables under the olive tree, lit by the trough and a line of bulbs. Tables of two to twenty-four, two and a half hours each. Book the garden; the counter is walk-in.

  • The counter, walk-in and pickupTue–Sun 12:00–16:00
  • The garden, bookedTue–Sun 18:00–00:00

06 Visit

Follow the smoke to Tanner's Row.

Through the green gate beside the old tannery chimney. The counter is on your left as you come in; the garden is through the arch. Bring an appetite and a jacket after ten.
